## Choose items

Connect to your repository. For restricted content, follow the authentication
vignette and log in before retrieving items.

```{r connect, eval=FALSE}
library(dspacer)

con <- ds_connect("https://repository.example.org/server/api")
collections <- ds_get_collections(con)
collections
```

Inspect the collection table, then retrieve items from a chosen collection:

```{r collection, eval=FALSE}
collection_id <- collections$collection_uuid[[1]]
items <- ds_get_items(con, scope = collection_id)
```

Other ways to choose items:

```{r alternatives, eval=FALSE}
# All visible archived search results, not just items owned by your account.
items <- ds_get_items(con)

# Search using your repository's Discovery query syntax.
items <- ds_get_items(con, query = "history")

# Retrieve known item UUIDs directly, without using the search index.
known_ids <- head(items$item_uuid, 2)
items <- ds_get_items(con, ids = known_ids)
```

Use `ids` instead of, not together with, `scope` or `query`.

## Extract metadata

The item table has one row per item. Its `metadata` list column preserves the
complete metadata map, including custom fields and repeated values.

```{r metadata, eval=FALSE}
metadata <- ds_get_metadata(items)
metadata
```

This produces one row per metadata value, retaining field names, languages,
authorities, confidence and ordering. Nothing is silently reduced to the first
value. Dates remain strings, including years, uncertain dates and non-Gregorian
dates.

`ds_get_metadata()` is a local transformation. It also accepts collection and
file tables; file metadata describes the attachment, not the parent item.
See `?ds_get_metadata` for the returned columns.

## Save a dataset

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(items = items, metadata = metadata), "repository_metadata.rds")
ds_disconnect(con)
```

Use repository URLs and UUIDs when joining datasets, not titles or filenames.
Network result tables carry a `dspacer` attribute recording repository/package
versions, the selection and retrieval start/end times. These records do not
make a live repository retrieval an atomic snapshot.

Search depends on the repository's index. Detected count changes or duplicate
UUIDs stop retrieval rather than silently claiming completeness; retry once the
repository is stable.
